title: AutoTracelet: catalog and adaptive dispatcher for low-friction support patches
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a lightweight catalog of small, composable support patches (AutoTracelets) plus an adaptive dispatcher that can suggest and, in safe modes, execute them automatically. Aim: reduce mean time to resolution for common support signals by enabling telemetry-driven, policy-gated shortflows that are auditable and reversible.
background: We already have ad-hoc shortflows and a prototype playbook runner. Support teams often write one-off scripts; this work generalizes those into typed, versioned artifacts (tracelets) with dispatcher heuristics that match incoming signals to candidates. Focus is on low-friction adoption: UI for ops to preview/approve, API for programmatic invocation, and observable rollout with canary policies.
goals: Define a canonical tracelet schema (inputs, outputs, idempotency signatures, rollback steps)
Implement a dispatcher service that ranks tracelet candidates given a telemetry event and context
Ship a minimal operator surface in Console: preview, dry-run, one-click apply with audit record
Ensure safety: RBAC gating, dry-run by default for new tracelets, automatic rollback tokens, and rate limits
Integrate telemetry & evals: measure MTTR delta and false-positive application rate
non_goals: Replacing full-runbook automation for complex incidents
Heavyweight orchestration for long-running multi-step repairs (this targets <120s fixes)
Implementing model-driven natural-language synthesis of tracelets in this phase
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Tracelets as small JSON/YAML manifests to keep them portable vs. embedding runtime code which would be more flexible but harder to audit
Dispatcher uses rule templates + a lightweight ML re-ranker (later) — start with deterministic heuristics for explainability
Execution modes: preview-only, operator-approved apply, and auto-apply with tight quotas. Auto-apply requires additional security review and per-customer opt-in
Rollback tokens are preferred over attempting to infer inverse actions for safety; authors must provide an explicit rollback step
Keep execution runtime language-agnostic: invoke containerized steps or run approved scripts in a sandboxed service to avoid dependency sprawl
acceptance_criteria: Tracelet schema documented and validated with unit tests
Dispatcher prototype returns ranked candidates for three canonical signals (OOM, high-latency query, KV-miss storm) with >80% relevant candidate in top-3
Console surface shows preview + diff + estimated cost and writes audit record on any apply
A safety matrix exists: RBAC roles required, QA checklist, and automated dry-run by default
Telemetry: initial experiment shows >=10% MTTR improvement on selected support alerts in pilot
implementation_outline: Dispatcher service: rule engine + candidate scoring API — 6d
Execution sandbox: containerized invoker with resource limits & rollback token plumbing — 8d
Console integration: preview UI, apply flow, audit log link — 5d
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misapplied tracelet causes customer impact. Mitigation: default to dry-run for first N deployments, require opt-in for auto-apply, per-tenant rate limits
Risk: tracelets diverge into unreviewed scripts. Mitigation: enforcement of signing + review process and CI gating for new tracelet manifests
Risk: dispatcher false positives. Mitigation: human-in-loop for top-ranked suggestions for first 30 days and telemetry-based retraining triggers
Risk: audit noise. Mitigation: compact, structured audit entries with links to playbook and deterministic replay for investigations
qa_plan: Unit tests for validator and dispatcher ranking rules
Integration tests: run tracelets in sandbox against synthetic telemetry fixtures
Canary rollout to internal ops team with opt-in for auto-apply on non-prod namespaces
Chaos test: inject failure in sandbox and ensure rollback token path is executed and recorded
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal ops only, preview/dry-run mode (2 weeks)
Beta: selected customers + opt-in auto-apply with daily caps (4 weeks)
GA: general availability when MTTR gains are validated and security review is passed
metrics: MTTR for alert classes where tracelets apply
Auto-apply error rate and rollback invocation rate
Audit latency (time between action and recorded audit entry)
next_steps: Finalize tracelet manifest RFC and circulate for review (Confluence link below)
Spin up a dispatcher PoC branch and wire three sample tracelets
Request security kickoff and threat model session with SecOps
Schedule a pilot with Oncall and Support (2-week window)
